design: A: one program per row; BLOCK_H=next_pow2(H); in-register f32 two-pass mean+population var (divisor H); host _ndtri scalar Z; bf16 in -> f32 compute -> bf16 out; 1 read + 1 write
hypothesis: Fused single-read/single-write bf16 kernel with f32 two-pass stats and host-precomputed _ndtri Z is correct within atol=1e-5/rtol=0.05 and yields a large multi-x speedup over the multi-kernel f32 reference (H1: ~5-8x traffic cut, bandwidth-bound).
notes: Correctness anchor / baseline. 5/5 PASSED, geomean 24.35x. WL1 (H=8192, largest, dominates weight) is the lowest speedup at 12.2x and the main remaining lever; its max_rel 0.167 is comfortably within the 99% matched-ratio tolerance. WL4 (H=4096) 19.4x next lowest. H=12288 rows (WL2/WL3) already ~36-40x -> no visible design-A register-spill penalty at num_warps=16. Next: tune num_warps/num_stages branching from c001, focusing on WL1.

design: A (same kernel as c001); single knob changed: uniform num_warps=16 for all H (raise the H<=8192 path from 8 -> 16).
hypothesis: H3/ILP lever: raising num_warps from 8 to 16 on the H<=8192 path halves per-thread element count (H=8192: 32->16 elems/thread) and increases parallel loads in flight, lifting WL1/WL4/WL5 without hurting the already-fast H=12288 path.
notes: 5/5 PASSED, geomean 24.93x (+2.4% over c001 24.35x). num_warps=16 uniform helped H=12288 (WL2 35.81->37.26, WL3 40.00->42.50) and WL5 (25.17->25.95); WL1 essentially flat (12.20->12.23, sol_ms 0.3532->0.3524); WL4 slightly DOWN (19.45->19.16, sol_ms 0.0825->0.0837). Correctness margins identical to c001. Accept as new best. Key insight: WL1 (M=18608 x H=8192, sol_ms 0.352 ms, 12.2x) is NOT moving with warps -> it is likely memory-bandwidth bound already, not ILP-bound; the fused kernel is near roofline for WL1. WL4 regressed slightly at warps=16 (fewer rows/SM residency at H=4096). Next lever candidates: (a) num_stages sweep to pipeline loads; (b) rows-per-program for small-H (WL4) to restore its warps=8-like residency; but WL1 (dominant) may be at roofline, capping further geomean gains.
